page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i5.12xlarge is an instance within the Local SSDs family designed for high-capacity local storage and memory-intensive processing. Running on the KVM hypervisor with an x86_64 architecture, this virtual machine features 48 dedicated vCPUs powered by Intel Xeon 6982P-C processors clocked at 3.4 GHz. System memory totals 384.0 GB, allocating 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware provisioning also bundles 11519 GB of local SSD capacity alongside a 120 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile.

The primary structural characteristic of the instance is its dense coupling of substantial local storage with high network throughput. Delivering over 11 terabytes of integrated SSD space directly attached to the host, it reduces external network volume overhead for data operations. A trade-off is the ephemeral nature typical of direct-attached local solid-state drives, which requires application-level data redundancy strategies to manage host failure risks. Furthermore, the configuration lacks dedicated GPU hardware accelerators and does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Cost efficiency is driven by the co-location of significant internal compute, substantial memory density, and massive local storage inside a single host footprint, reducing the need to provision decoupled network-attached block storage for scratch or replica storage. Suitable workloads include large-scale relational databases, NoSQL data stores, distributed search clusters, big data processing engines, and transactional analytics platforms requiring rapid access to vast local data sets.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i5.12xlarge is an x86_64 storage-optimized instance tailored for demanding enterprise workloads. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs driven by an Intel Xeon 6982P-C processor operating at 3.4 GHz, combined with 384.0 GB of system memory at an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. The configuration integrates 11519 GB of direct-attached local SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 120 Gbps managed via KVM virtualization. With no discrete GPU acceleration, the platform relies purely on CPU compute and memory-to-storage bandwidth. The combination of dense local storage and extensive network capacity makes the instance effective for distributed NoSQL databases, transactional engines, data indexing clusters, and high-throughput real-time processing pipelines.
